title: Emergency Ambulance Routing
short_description: Learn how an emergency-response system models roads as a graph to route an ambulance to a hospital while minimizing travel time or distance.

real_world_context.problem: An emergency-response system must identify an efficient route from an ambulance location to a hospital. The road network is modeled as a graph where intersections are nodes and roads are edges carrying travel time or distance. The system must explore reachable areas, confirm a route exists, find the fastest path, guide the search toward the hospital, and decide which hospitals are reachable within a maximum allowed travel time.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Every second matters in an emergency. Modeling the road network as a graph and choosing the right algorithm helps the system send an ambulance along the fastest possible route to the nearest reachable hospital.

learning_objectives: Understand how a road network can be represented as a graph for emergency response.
Use Graph BFS to explore areas reachable from the ambulance location.
Use Graph DFS to detect whether a route to a hospital exists.
Use Dijkstra's Algorithm to find the fastest route to a hospital by travel time.
Use A* Pathfinding to guide the search toward the hospital with a heuristic.
Use Binary Search on Answer to find hospitals reachable within a maximum travel time budget.
completion_message: You have completed the Emergency Ambulance Routing mission. You have learned how graph traversal, weighted shortest-path, guided search and binary-search-on-answer techniques help an emergency-response system route an ambulance to a hospital efficiently.
